address: Nieuwendijk / Dirk van Hasseltssteeg, Amsterdam: 1997 H&M department store block behind retained house fronts
notes: H&M Nieuwendijk / Dirk van Hasseltssteeg 20-28 (BAG), a 1997 H&M department-store complex built behind retained and rebuilt Nieuwendijk fronts: two linked blocks (the footprint is 4,152 m2 with 700 3DBAG wall surfaces) whose exposed street walls are the curved glass shopfront on the SE (panel 84, w05-115, 2019-12-20), a cream rendered front (panel 9, w06-123, 2021-03-11), the dark brick and white-framed house fronts on the Dirk van Hasseltssteeg (panel 106, w02-174, 2025-01-20) and a glass-and-grey corner (panel 113, w04-182, 2016-08-15).

Modelled: three groups on three of the four photographed walls (the fourth, the glass corner panel 113, is left blank: its eaves 13.1 m disagree with the 11.8 m roof behind it and fail the eaves gate), storeys and bays counted from the crops; punched bays on all floors. Simplified: the curved glass shopfront is straight glazed bays on the 3DBAG plane (LoD2.2 has it as flat facets), the perforated timber-lattice balcony screens over the shop are plain wall, the historic gables behind are 3DBAG massing only. Not modelled: the red H&M sign (entrance component's frames fail the z-fight gate so no entrance or lettering is drawn; add entrance + signage H&M to walls[0] once frames are 3 cm proud), the shop interiors visible behind the glass, the Cola/Gelato signs on the steeg houses, the blank north block (no photograph).
Walls with no panorama (N side, the interior block, party walls) stay blank.

GATE STATUS: authored but NOT installable. `open-edges` fails (6 edges, 54.2 m) because the 3DBAG LoD2.2 shell itself has a ~0.7 m wide, 16 m tall wall gap near local x 14-16, z -18; dropping any wall group leaves it at 54.16 m. Needs a shell-gap sealer in the block kit (not written) or a corrected 3DBAG item.
